claims.text: Before combining, Git works out the merge base — the newest commit reachable from both tips (a tangled history can have more than one; here there is exactly one). For `main` and `feature/shipping` in the playground it is 09c8526.
claims.source_hint: gitglossary, entry 'merge base'; git-merge-base documentation, DESCRIPTION

claims.text: `git merge <branch>` combines the changes each side made since the merge base and, unless the merge resolves as a fast-forward, records the result in one new commit whose parents are the commit HEAD was on, listed first, and the tip of the named branch, listed second.
claims.source_hint: git-merge documentation, DESCRIPTION and 'TRUE MERGE'; git-commit-tree documentation on parent order

claims.text: A merge writes only the new commit: every commit on both sides keeps its id, and the branch named in the command still points at the same commit afterwards.
claims.source_hint: git-merge documentation, DESCRIPTION ('the current branch is updated'); outputs/stage-0/scripts/git/merge-demo.txt last two lines

claims.text: When the current branch has no commits of its own since the merge base, `git merge` by default performs a fast-forward: it writes no new commit and updates HEAD, the index and the working tree to the named commit.
claims.source_hint: git-merge documentation, 'FAST-FORWARD MERGE' and --ff/--no-ff

claims.text: `git rebase <upstream>` replays the current branch's commits not in <upstream>, in order: the first on <upstream>, each next on the commit the previous replay wrote; each gets a new parent and therefore a new id, and the branch is moved to the last one written.
claims.source_hint: git-rebase documentation, DESCRIPTION ('commits are reapplied on top of'); gitglossary, entry 'rebase'

claims.text: The commits a rebase replaced are not deleted at once: they remain in the repository until Git removes objects nothing points at, which is why an id from before a rebase still resolves for a time.
claims.source_hint: git-gc documentation, DESCRIPTION (unreachable objects and gc.pruneExpire); git-rebase documentation, RECOVERING FROM UPSTREAM REBASE

claims.text: Rebasing commits that were already pushed makes the branch disagree with the copy on the server: pushing it requires a force option, and a repository that had fetched the old commits keeps both versions of the same work.
claims.source_hint: git-rebase documentation, RECOVERING FROM UPSTREAM REBASE; git-push documentation, --force/--force-with-lease and non-fast-forward rejection

claims.text: `git switch -c <name> <start-point>` creates a branch named <name> at <start-point> and makes it the current branch.
claims.source_hint: git-switch documentation, -c/--create and <start-point>

claims.text: `git merge --no-edit` accepts the commit message Git composes for the merge instead of opening an editor to change it.
claims.source_hint: git-merge documentation, --edit/--no-edit

claims.text: In `git show --format`, `%h` is the abbreviated commit id, `%s` the subject line, `%p` the abbreviated parent ids separated by a space, and `--no-patch` suppresses the diff.
claims.source_hint: git-log documentation, PRETTY FORMATS (%h, %s, %p); git-show documentation, -s/--no-patch

claims.text: `git log --oneline --graph` draws a merge commit with a `|\` line beneath it opening two columns, `* |` for a commit on one column while the other runs past it, and `|/` where the columns rejoin at the shared commit; a history with no merge prints one `*` per line and no `|` column.
claims.source_hint: git-log documentation, --graph and --oneline

claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang at stage-0: outputs/stage-0/scripts/git/merge-demo.txt, the 'two parents' and 'untouched' blocks; git-playground/build-history.sh for the pinned identity and dates

claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang at stage-0: outputs/stage-0/scripts/git/rebase-demo.txt, the before/after id blocks and the final graph

claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang at stage-0: outputs/stage-0/scripts/git/rebase-demo.txt line 2 (the --decorate listing)

claims.text: Git 2.46 combines the two sides with a named strategy; the captured merge reports `Merge made by the 'ort' strategy.`, ort being the strategy Git chooses by default for a merge of two branches.
claims.source_hint: git-merge documentation, MERGE STRATEGIES ('ort' as the default); outputs/stage-0/scripts/git/merge-demo.txt line 1

claims.text: Both `git merge` and `git rebase` stop and hand the work back to you when the two sides changed the same region; a rebase can stop once per commit it replays, because it applies them one at a time.
claims.source_hint: git-merge documentation, HOW CONFLICTS ARE PRESENTED; git-rebase documentation, DESCRIPTION (stopping on each applied commit, --continue/--abort)

claims.text: Opinion: a merge keeps the fork visible while a rebase leaves one column; a common team rule is to pick one shape for a whole repository, so a reader learns one shape instead of working out which rule held for each stretch.
claims.source_hint: outline item 4 of foundation.l2.git-merge-vs-rebase

claims.text: Opinion: when a branch has already been pushed and others may hold it, merging is the safer of the two, because merge only adds a commit while rebase replaces commits those repositories already have.
claims.source_hint: outline item 2 of foundation.l2.git-merge-vs-rebase; git-rebase documentation, RECOVERING FROM UPSTREAM REBASE

claims.text: A commit's id is computed from its content, and its parent is part of that content; this lesson reuses that fact from foundation.l2.git-mental-model to explain why replayed commits get new ids.
claims.source_hint: gitglossary, entries 'commit' and 'object name'; foundation.l2.git-mental-model summary line 4

claims.text: `git log --decorate` prints the names that point at a commit in parentheses beside it.
claims.source_hint: git-log documentation, --decorate[=short|full|auto|no]

claims.text: A rebase is undone by putting the branch name back on the commit it pointed at before: Git records that tip in ORIG_HEAD and in the branch's reflog, and the replaced commits stay in the repository until unreachable objects are removed.
claims.source_hint: git-rebase documentation, DESCRIPTION (ORIG_HEAD is set to the pre-rebase tip) and NOTES ('the previous branch tip ... is accessible using the reflog'); git-gc documentation on unreachable objects
